_label: FIXTURE: hypothetical demo meeting between Charan Rathore (lead) and Harsh Sinha (teammate), written from the team's real build decisions on 2026-11-15. Both consented. Not a Wispr Notetaker record.

meeting.title: Kaam Ki Baat — kickoff and architecture

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Okay Harsh, we have three hours. Before we touch code, let's agree what we start with: one problem, one user, one demo.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Agreed. So what exactly is the problem?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Teams decide things in meetings and then lose them. A week later nobody can say who owns it, whether the code exists, whether the PR is merged, or whether the tests passed on the latest commit.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: And then someone pings the lead and waits.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Exactly. The user is an engineer on a small team, like you, sitting on a doubt that blocks the task. The other user is the lead, like me, answering the same question for the fifth time.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Is this really common, or is it just us?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: It's common. Microsoft's Work Trend Index says 55% of people find next steps unclear after meetings. Atlassian's developer experience report says 69% of developers lose eight or more hours a week to inefficiencies.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: And Stack Overflow's survey says 61% spend more than half an hour a day just searching for answers. So the waiting is the real cost.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Right. So the solution: a voice teammate. Wispr Flow gives us what was said in the meeting, GitHub gives us what was built, and Bolna lets you just call and ask.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: How do we stop it from making things up?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Fixed rules decide status, not the model. Proposed is not accepted, an open PR is not merged, and a check on an older commit is stale. If it doesn't know, it asks the leader instead of guessing.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: And the three agents?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Left is Team Memory, for what we decided. Front is the Leader Desk, which only I can open, from my laptop with Touch ID. Right is the Code Navigator, which uses a graph of the repo to point at the exact file, function and line.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: A head turn picks one, and I can also press A for left and L for right?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Yes. But turning your head only selects an agent. It never proves who you are.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: One more rule: the agent says saved only after the update is read back from the store. A timeout is a failure.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: That reminds me, on yesterday's test call it said saved even though the write had timed out.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Then that's your first task. You own the fix. Start from persistVerifiedUpdate and check the timeout and the read-back.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Okay, I'll take the saved-after-timeout bug.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Can you also run the three test calls, each longer than 45 seconds, with an evaluation note after each one?

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Yes, I'll run the three calls and write the notes.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: I'll handle the leader approvals during the demo.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Should the code graph agent move to the left side?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Maybe. Let's decide after the first call.

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Someone should record the demo film before four. Not sure who yet.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Last thing: do we freeze the code at 3:30 or 3:45?

passages.speaker: Charan
passages.text: Let's not decide that now. Ask me through the agent later, that's a good test.

passages.speaker: Harsh
passages.text: Okay. I'm on board with the whole plan. Let's test it now and see what I actually understood.
